sources.name: Web Coverage Service 2.1 Core (OGC 17-089r1)
verified_facts: WCS 2.1 is the OGC core standard for Internet access to multi-dimensional coverages.
The core standard defines service behavior while extensions complete response encoding and processing behavior.
WCS 2.1 extends WCS 2.0 backwards-compatibly to support CIS 1.1 coverages.
semantic_limits: A successful WCS request proves protocol-level access, not parcel-level elevation correctness.
Coverage identifier, DescribeCoverage metadata and returned bytes must be read back together.

sources.name: Coverage Implementation Schema 1.1.1 (OGC 09-146r8)
verified_facts: CIS 1.1 defines a conformance-testable coverage structure with DomainSet, RangeSet and RangeType.
Each direct position must correspond to exactly one range value.
Unknown or absent values require declared nil values and range values must match the RangeType structure.
semantic_limits: Nil or nodata cells must be excluded from parcel min/max calculations rather than treated as terrain height.
Coverage structural conformance does not establish source vertical accuracy.

sources.name: GeoTIFF 1.1 Standard (OGC 19-008r4)
verified_facts: GeoTIFF 1.1 defines TIFF tags for georeferenced raster imagery and aligns CRS identifiers with the EPSG dataset.
A GeoTIFF must carry raster-to-model positioning through ModelTiepointTag or ModelTransformationTag under the specified rules.
GeoKeyDirectoryTag is mandatory and byte order must be honoured by readers.
semantic_limits: A valid GeoTIFF container does not prove that the raster contains EA DTM 1 m or ODN heights.
CRS keys, affine transform, dimensions, nodata semantics and source hash require independent readback.

sources.name: Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF 1.0 Standard (OGC 21-026)
verified_facts: COG organizes GeoTIFF content to support efficient extraction of required regions and resolutions.
The standard defines HTTP range request conformance for retrieving only portions of large files.
COG depends on the GeoTIFF standard and does not replace GeoTIFF georeferencing requirements.
semantic_limits: A partial HTTP range response must not be mistaken for proof that the full source file or required tile was validated.
Byte-range efficiency does not improve source resolution, vertical accuracy or parcel binding.
